summary: Wythe County, VA USFS tower: 81-ft timber tower built 1939, taken down 1973; register says concrete footers and a cistern remain; county disputed (Grayson per firelookout.org).

facts.status_note: Taken down in 1973 per register and Forest Lookouts; register says concrete footers and a small cistern remain

events.note: Taken down in 1973 per register; Forest Lookouts lists '1973: Removed'
Registered November 13, 2010 as US 726, VA 6; nominated by Dan East

evidence.supports: firelookout.org lists the county as Grayson
evidence.quote: Jones Knob Grayson 36.76579 -81.07284 Tower Gone FFLOS US 726, VA 6
This 81' treated timber tower was constructed in 1939 and was taken down in 1973.

evidence.supports: tower served the southern part of Wythe County and watched for fires around Cripple Creek
evidence.quote: This tower served the southern portion of Wythe County, and was used to watch for forest fires around the Cripple Creek area of the county.

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts marks the tower removed in 1973
concrete footers and a small cistern still remain
evidence.quote: The 18'3" concrete footers and a small cistern still remain.

evidence.supports: cistern at the center of the four footers
evidence.quote: The cistern sits in the exact center of the 4 footers.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and Forest Lookouts both say Wythe County; the firelookout.org Virginia list says Grayson. The story follows Wythe and says the sources differ. Coordinates were not checked against county boundaries.

notes_for_editor: The county disagreement is unresolved and should be checked against a county map before publishing. A 1951 Appalachian Trail Histories photo caption (https://www.appalachiantrailhistory.org/items/show/1156) mentions a view 'from the Jones Knob lookout, possibly from the fire tower that used to stand there'; its timing is unclear against the 1973 removal and it is marked 'All rights reserved', so it is not used as a photo or fact. No staffing or fire record found in the sources read. Access not described.
